ops.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. REGULATION: the EU AI Act 'Digital Omnibus' simplification is on track for formal Parliament adoption (~7 July 2026) and entry into force by end of July 2026, confirming the prior scan's Council sign-off — the Annex III high-risk deadline stays 2 Dec 2027 and the content-labelling deadline stays 2 Dec 2026, and a new prohibition (AI-generated CSAM / non-consensual intimate material) was added; the SME carve-out (≤750 staff/€150M revenue) is confirmed, not yet relevant at this scale. AUSTRALIA: unchanged — mandatory guardrails remain formally abandoned (Dec 2025 National AI Plan), voluntary guidance plus an advisory-only AI Safety Institute persist, and the OAIC's automated-decision consultation closed 15 June with formal guidance due September 2026 ahead of the 10 Dec 2026 APP 1.7–1.9 deadline. FUNDING: AI now captures ~50% of pre-seed dollars (up from ~30%), the seed premium holds at 42%, and the market is consolidating toward larger checks (sub-$1M rounds shrinking as a share) — a continuing headwind for a small, unconnected raise. SOLO-FOUNDER: 36% of new US startups are solo-founded; 29.8M US solopreneurs generate $1.7T in revenue; the cheap AI-ops-stack thesis keeps validating. AGENTIC OPS: agentic AI is now in ~72% of production AI deployments with 40% of enterprise apps incorporating agents by year-end, and commentary flags governance lagging adoption; notably, Lyzr ran its own $100M Series B fundraise through its own AI agent — a direct proof-of-concept for the 'use our own products for operational intelligence' principle. RISK: EU labelling (Dec 2026) and AU APP (Dec 2026) deadlines approach but aren't urgent; the industry-wide agent-governance gap is a general risk to watch. OPPORTUNITY: the solo-founder AI stack and self-dogfooding precedent both directly validate the Sage Ops approach.

tech.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. NEXT.JS — ACTION-WORTHY: the first formal Next.js Security Release lands today, 20 July 2026, patching the 16.2.x and 15.5.x branches for 4 high- and 5 medium-severity vulnerabilities — worth confirming the deployed Next.js version and applying the patch promptly; it also carries stale-ISR-revalidation, manifest.ts HMR, and Turbopack stability fixes. Next.js 16.3 Preview adds instant navigations, partial prefetching, and further Turbopack memory/cache gains — no action needed there yet. ANTHROPIC: Claude Sonnet 5 (GA 30 June) remains the configured model, no re-pin needed (PR4); Claude Fable 5 resumed global redeployment 1 July after its export-control suspension lifted; Claude Code shipped a stability/safety update (tighter permission checks, safer Bash/PowerShell handling, an EndConversation tool, progress heartbeats for long tasks) directly relevant to the project's own Claude Code session and hooks work. TYPESCRIPT — ACTION-WORTHY: TypeScript 7.0 (the Go-native 'tsgo' compiler) reached GA on 8 July 2026, folded into the standard `typescript`/`tsc` package with real-world 8–12x speedups (VS Code's own type-check: 125.7s→10.6s) — a plausible drop-in win for the project's `tsc 0` verification gates, though it ships without a stable programmatic API in 7.0 (some ecosystem tooling may lag until 7.1) and Vue/Svelte support isn't there yet, so a scoped trial rather than a blanket upgrade is the sound move. SUPABASE: pricing and features unchanged this scan (Free/$25 Pro/$599 Team). LLM COST TRENDS: frontier output pricing is down ~94.5% since March 2023; inference now runs only 30–45% of a typical AI product's total cost (down from 70–80% two years ago), so further inference-only optimisation has diminishing returns — consonant with the project's model-selection-as-constraint discipline. SECURITY: no new Supabase Auth/Vercel CVEs surfaced this scan (a March-disclosed, already-patched Supabase Auth Apple/Azure-OIDC bypass, CVE-2026-31813, is old news and likely inapplicable unless those providers are enabled). OPPORTUNITY: both the Next.js security patch and a scoped TypeScript 7.0 trial are concrete near-term wins for the CI/verification loop.

growth.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. MCP (most material): the Model Context Protocol's final specification release candidate is due 28 July 2026, making the protocol stateless at the connection layer — worth a close read once final, given the project's design-for-interop MCP posture (R18c). ECOSYSTEM: still eight marketplaces that matter for distribution, with the trend continuing from fragmented directories toward curated marketplaces that compete on security, quality-curation, and creator economics — reinforcing the prior scan's preference for the Anthropic-native directory/observability path over scattered third-party listings (PR15). DEVREL: 'agent experience' is now fully mainstream practice — the LLM is treated as the first-touch user of any API/docs, 'agent skills are the new demos,' and API design is explicitly framed as a DevRel problem — directly validating the project's llms.txt/agent-card.json/skill-contract investment as on-trend. Developers are also increasingly starting product research on ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity rather than Google (Generative Engine Optimization), a channel shift worth factoring into any future content strategy. COMPETITORS: the AI-ethics-tooling field stays fragmented and mostly enterprise-bias/fairness-focused (IBM AI Fairness 360, Deon, FairAI Toolkit, Fujitsu's AI Ethics Impact Assessment); no new entrant surfaced this scan competing on a Stoic-character/virtue-trust framing — the honesty-under-pressure gap noted in prior scans remains open. STOIC COMMUNITY: continued growth (Reddit/X ~400% YoY content growth; Stoic Week 2026 drew 3,300+ participants from 40+ countries; The Daily Stoic's Instagram sits at 3M followers), with commentary explicitly tying the surge to tech-industry burnout — a relevant signal for the developer/agent-builder audience segment. RISK: 'Stoicism' dilution/meme-ification online continues; the MCP finalisation may warrant an interop compatibility check once the RC lands. OPPORTUNITY: the agent-experience/DevRel trend and the still-open honesty-framing gap both favour current positioning.

support.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. REGULATORY CONVERGENCE (most material): China introduced companion-chatbot rules on 15 July 2026 requiring emotional-distress detection, crisis intervention, usage limits, and user data control — a global (not just US/EU) regulatory pattern now converging on essentially the architecture R20a already implements, reinforcing that this posture tracks an emerging international norm, not a single jurisdiction's preference. LEGAL ESCALATION: Florida's first-in-the-nation state lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman (filed 1 June 2026, alleging profit-over-safety design, addictive engagement, and links to a mass shooting and suicides) and the 42-state AG subpoena naming sycophancy explicitly are both still live and developing — both raise the general reputational stakes for anything in the 'AI companion' category, reinforcing the value of clear distance from that framing. The UN AI Report's sycophancy-death findings now anchor the first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance (opened Geneva 6 July) — an institutional escalation from research-level to UN-level attention. EVIDENCE FOR HONEST POSITIONING: a new APA survey finds 94% of psychologists have concerns about patients using AI chatbots as a mental-health resource, and The Lancet describes AI-therapist clinical effectiveness as 'insufficiently established' — both externally validate the R19c/R19d honest-limitations, non-therapy positioning as increasingly evidence-backed. STATE LAW: Connecticut's Public Act 26-15 (signed 2 June) requires chatbot operators to detect suicidal ideation and maintain response protocols, reinforcing the existing R20a design; California's SB 243 baseline is already in effect, with further requirements not due until 1 July 2027. ACCESSIBILITY: unchanged — WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA remains the live target; WCAG 3.0's next working draft is due ~September 2026, finalisation not expected before 2028. RISK: the regulatory floor keeps rising quickly (China, Florida, Connecticut, the UN) — worth a periodic R20a/R19 posture re-check, though nothing here requires immediate action. OPPORTUNITY: the psychologist-concern and Lancet findings make the honest, non-sycophantic, redirect-first stance a stronger, better-evidenced differentiator.
